steps: Open Agents and click Get to know a host, or ask Claude about a host from its Map card.
Pick the host you want a briefing on.
Read what it serves, how it is built, how it signs users in and which requests to look at first.
Pick a request in Traffic.
Click Ask Claude in the Lens, or open Agents and click Explain a request with its number.
Read the walk-through: what the request does, and what its tokens and encoded values hold.
Sign in to the app once while Plonix captures, so the sign-in requests are there.
Open Agents and click Review sign-in and sessions.
Read which requests sign in and out, which cookie or token keeps you signed in, and what to test next.
Browse the target for a while so Scope has suggested domains.
Open Agents and click Check scope suggestions.
Accept or reject each domain yourself in Scope. The agent only recommends.
Find something worth reporting and note the requests that show it.
Open Agents and click Draft a finding report, describing the issue in a line.
Review the draft, then record it in Findings yourself.
Install it, then use the API's client or browse the app so its calls are captured.
Open Agents and click Inventory an API, then pick the API host.
Work through the table of operations it returns, with their parameters, sign-in and data.
Install it once: it brings the API inventory skill, the leak filters and admin console detection.
In Traffic, filter with is:aws-keys, is:jwts or is:stack-traces to find leaks.
Open Agents and click Inventory an API for a table of every operation.
Install trufflehog on your Mac (brew install trufflehog).
Install secret-sweep and allow it to run trufflehog.
Click Check captured traffic on this page once. New traffic is checked as it arrives.
Open a request in Traffic: every key or token it found shows in the Lens as a Spotted chip with its name.
Install js-endpoints. Nothing else is needed.
Browse the app so its JavaScript files are captured. Their hosts must be in scope, or it skips them.
Click Read captured traffic on this page once. New files are read as they arrive.
Open a JavaScript file in Traffic: the Lens lists the API paths and URLs the script mentions. Send one to the Bench to try it.
Install subfinder on your Mac (brew install subfinder).
Install subdomain-discovery and allow it to run subfinder.
Accept your target's domain in Scope, for example example.com.
Click Find subdomains in Scope, or on this page. It asks public sources and adds what it finds as suggestions.
Accept or reject each suggestion in Scope. Nothing joins your scope until you do.
Install parameter-probe and allow it to send its requests.
In Traffic, right-click an in-scope request and choose Probe for hidden parameters. Or paste an address on this page.
It sends about a hundred requests, one per parameter name, each recorded in Traffic.
Names that change the response show in the result and in an unconfirmed finding for you to check.
Not built yet. Until it is, filter Traffic with is:graphql to see GraphQL requests, and open one in the Lens.
Install security-headers. Nothing else is needed.
Browse the app's pages, or click Read captured traffic on this page once.
Open an HTML page in Traffic: the Lens notes each missing header and each cookie without Secure or HttpOnly.
Findings gets one unconfirmed finding per host. Confirm or dismiss it there.
Built in and always on. Open a host in Map to see its web server under Technologies.
Built in and always on. Open a host in Map to see the languages and frameworks it runs on.
Built in and always on. Open a host in Map to see whether it runs a content management system or shop platform.
Built in and always on. Open a host in Map to see the CDN, WAF or cache in front of it.
Built in and always on. Open a host in Map to see API styles, API documentation and identity endpoints it found.
Install it. It works on traffic you already have and everything captured later.
Open a host in Map: an exposed console such as Jenkins, Grafana or phpMyAdmin shows under Technologies.
Built in. In Traffic, click + Filter and pick one, or type is:api, is:auth, is:admin or is:trackers in the search box.
Install it.

In Traffic, click + Filter, or type a filter in the search box: is:aws-keys, is:jwts, is:private-keys, is:stack-traces, is:java-traces, is:sql-errors, is:debug-pages, is:source-maps or is:internal-ips.
Each shows only the requests whose text matches it.
Built in. On the Bench, switch to Run, point at a value to vary and choose From a list.
Install it.
On the Bench, switch to Run, point at a value to vary and choose From a list.
Pick Identifier formats, Common ports or API paths.
Install it. A Users screen appears in the sidebar.
Add each account you test with: its cookies or token, copied from a request where it was signed in.
On the Bench, pick who to send as from the As… menu, or act as a user everywhere from the title bar.
Install it with Saved users, and save at least two users.
Pick requests in Traffic and choose Replay signed out or Check this id across users, or open Access and pick a host.
Read the table: each request as each user and signed out, with what looks wrong flagged under it.
Install interactsh on your Mac (brew install interactsh), then install Callbacks.
Open Callbacks, press Start listening, then click New host for a test.
Put the host in a request on the Bench, such as a URL parameter or a webhook field, and send it.
Anything that reaches the host shows in Callbacks, with the test it belongs to.
Install it. A Programs screen appears in the sidebar.
Connect HackerOne with your own token, paste a program's policy, or look up a domain's security.txt.
Review a program, then follow it: its assets become scope rules and its rules are kept while you test.
Install Programs first.
In Programs, connect HackerOne with your API username and token.
Every program you can hack on is listed and searchable by name or asset.

mind-reader.where: Traffic, in the Lens and on right-click
steps: Built in and always on.
Open a request in Traffic: when Plonix recognises a shape, such as a token, an XML body or a GraphQL call, the Lens offers the next step as a chip.
Click the chip to run it. Nothing runs until you do.
